title: The timeout that wasn't a stalled stream
description: A first-fault snapshot exposed a timestamp race. R41 then sustained silent streaming, while audible output remained a separate test.
evidenceLabel: Compiled race regression and physical streaming
summary: The stream reported no progress shortly after a completed block. Capturing the state before shutdown showed that the timeout calculation could read its two timestamps in the wrong order.

timeline.title: Preserve the fault before changing the stream

sections.title: Qualify the transport before asking for sound
paragraphs: The original audio application started with output disabled. Its first active test moved zero-valued data, which let us examine the stream without treating an audible waveform as the only sign of progress. R38 reached its DMA interrupt handler, caught a transmit FIFO error and stopped before counting a healthy block. The USB writer remained responsive.

Empty transmit FIFOs at startup were a plausible cause, but the record did not capture the timing needed to prove it. R39 tested that hypothesis by filling the FIFOs with zeros before enabling the stream. It kept the existing fault checks. The physical attempt advanced through 31 healthy block completions before a different error, a no-progress timeout, stopped it.

sections.title: Save first-fault state before cleanup destroys it
paragraphs: R39's clean flags described its last completed interrupt, not necessarily the later moment when the timeout fired. They could not exclude a fault after that interrupt or explain why progress appeared to stop. Repeating the same test would not recover the missing state.

R40 added a fixed first-fault snapshot before shutting down the audio hardware. It recorded the relevant DMA, FIFO and interrupt state without clearing the fault on read. Its physical attempt counted thirteen healthy blocks, then reported the timeout again. The snapshot began only 71 timer ticks after the latest block, with DMA still active and no reported DMA error. That interval directed attention to the timeout calculation itself.
sections.checkpoint: A status captured during the last good event cannot fully describe a later failure. Preserve the failure state before resetting the subsystem.

sections.title: Two valid reads can form an impossible interval
paragraphs: R40 read the current timer first, then the timestamp of the latest completed block. An interrupt could finish a block between those reads and update the latter timestamp. The calculation would then subtract a newer timestamp from an older current-time sample. In unsigned arithmetic, that small negative difference becomes a very large elapsed interval.

R41 reads the last-block timestamp before reading the current clock. A deterministic test ran both compiled images with the problematic interrupt interleaving: it reproduced the R40 timeout and kept R41 running. Separate checks retained genuine-timeout behavior and handled timer rollover. The correction therefore addressed the read order without removing the timeout that detects real loss of progress.

sections.title: Keep the model result separate from the hardware result
paragraphs: R41's installation passed full occupied-sector readback and a separately opened status check. After the owner reported restarting, a fresh USB identity confirmed the new build with audio off and an idle writer. Those checks established the test baseline; the compiled race regression alone could not establish sustained physical streaming.

The silent run advanced through separated observations and ultimately reached 44,998 blocks without an audio, DMA, FIFO or sync fault. A single bounded waveform request also completed, and its timed lease returned the link to idle without error. The owner changed focus before reporting audibility or pressing pad 1. We therefore recorded sustained transport and a completed bounded request, while leaving headphone routing and pad-triggered sound unconfirmed.
steps: Confirm the corrected build after a real restart.
Observe silent progress across separate checks.
Keep the bounded waveform result distinct from a listening report.
Retain the failed binaries and snapshots alongside the correction.

sections.title: Reproduce the unsigned timeout in memory
paragraphs: The exercise uses an invented eight-bit timer so wraparound fits on one line. It supplies the two reads from the bad interleaving, then checks an ordered pair, a real timeout and a legitimate timer rollover. The bit width and numbers are teaching values, not the device's measured clock.

Reading the timestamps in the corrected order addresses this particular race. It does not prove that any two shared values are safe to read independently, or that a sequential fault snapshot is instantaneous while DMA continues. R41's physical result extends the evidence beyond the CPU model, but it still does not establish sampler features, audio quality or an audible output route.

exercise.title: Make a false timeout visible
exercise.intro: Run this Python 3 model of an invented wrapping timer. It has no device input, network operations or file writes.
exercise.code:
mask = 0xFF
threshold = 20

def elapsed(now, last):
    return (now - last) & mask

cases = [
    ('racing reads', 100, 101),
    ('ordered reads', 102, 99),
    ('real timeout', 140, 99),
    ('timer rollover', 3, 250),
]
for name, now, last in cases:
    age = elapsed(now, last)
    print(f'{name}: age={age}, timeout={age > threshold}')

assert elapsed(100, 101) > threshold
assert elapsed(102, 99) <= threshold
assert elapsed(140, 99) > threshold
assert elapsed(3, 250) == 9
exercise.expected:
racing reads: age=255, timeout=True
ordered reads: age=3, timeout=False
real timeout: age=41, timeout=True
timer rollover: age=9, timeout=False
exercise.explanation: The example exposes the arithmetic consequence of a stale current-time read. The real correction also had compiled interleaving tests and a later physical silent-stream result.

sources.title: R41 physical silent stream
sources.evidence: Retained project record: 44,998 silent blocks, completed bounded request and explicit absence of an audibility or pad-trigger result.

limits: Sustained silent streaming does not establish audible output or a headphone route.
The bounded waveform request completed, but the owner did not report listening results.
No pad-triggered sound result was recorded.
The first-fault snapshot was a sequence of bounded reads, not an instantaneous capture of moving hardware.
